summary: Raghunath Giri was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Vamacharana Bhattacharya. He held a post as department head (科長) at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith and taught Atsushi Uno.

Rahul Peter Das is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Cologne and Hamburg under Klaus Ludwig Janert and Albrecht Wezler, later serving as Professor of South Asian Studies at Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg (1994–2020).

Rahul Sankrityayan was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and Tibetologist. He taught Sanskrit at Vidyalankara Pirivena (1927) and later taught at the University of Saint Petersburg (1937, and as professor 1945–1947).

Raimo Anttila was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied under Warren Cowgill at Yale University (~1961–1966) and held positions at the University of California, Los Angeles (1965) and the University of Helsinki (1971–1976).

Raimon Panikkar was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Complutense University under Juan Zaragüeta, later teaching at Complutense (1946–1953), Harvard (1967–1971), and UC Santa Barbara (1971–1978).

Raimond Gaita is a philosopher who studied at the University of Melbourne and the University of Leeds. He served as Professor of Moral Philosophy at King's College London (1977–2011) and Foundation Professor of Philosophy at Australian Catholic University (1993–2011).

Raja Ram Shastri worked in Indology and was a Member of the Lok Sabha (~1971–1977). He also served as Chairman of the Managing Committee at Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University, attested in 1976.

Rajan Gurukkal is a historian who studied at the University of Calicut and Jawaharlal Nehru University. He served as Director of the School of Social Sciences at Mahatma Gandhi University (1988) and as a visiting professor at multiple institutions.

Rajan Khatiwoda is an Indology and history/archaeology researcher. He served as a research assistant and cataloguer for the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project (~2004–2013) and was an editorial board member for Documenta Nepalica (~2014).
Rajanaka Mahesvara was an Indology scholar who served as Departmental Pandit and Pandit at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir, attested in 1923 and 1925.
Rajaram Hegde is a scholar in history, archaeology, and religious studies. Attested in 2010, he served as Director at Kuvempu University and at the Centre for the Study of Local Cultures.

Rajendra Chandra Hazra was an Indologist who completed his BA and doctoral studies under Sushil Kumar De at Dhaka University. He taught at Dhaka University (1939–1951) and was Associate Professor of Smrti and Purāņa at Sanskrit College (1951–1972).

Rajendralal Mitra was an Indologist and historian educated at Kolkata institutions including Medical College. He served as librarian-cum-assistant-secretary (1846–1856) and president (1885) of The Asiatic Society, and directed Wards' Institution (1856–1881).

Rajkrishna Mukhopadhyay was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Krishnagar Government College and Presidency University (~1864–1866). He later held posts at Presidency University and Scottish Church College.
Raju Rimal is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. Attested in 2018, he held posts at the National Archives of Nepal and served as an editorial board member for Documenta Nepalica.

Rakhal Das Banerji was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at Presidency College and the University of Calcutta. He was an officer at the Archaeological Survey of India (1911–1926) and Manindra Chandra Nandy Professor at Banaras Hindu University (1928–1930).
Rakra Tethong Rinpoche studied under the guidance of Gendun Chopel and Trijang Rinpoche.

Ralf Kramer is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and at the University of London. He has served as Tibetan librarian at the Indian Institute, Oxford, and Aris Librarian at the Bodleian Library.

Ralph Abraham was a scholar in mathematics and philosophy who completed his degrees at the University of Michigan and studied under Debabrata Sensharma. He held posts at Berkeley, Columbia, and Princeton, and was Professor at UC Santa Cruz (1980).

Ralph Lerner is a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Chicago (~1945–1953) under Leo Strauss (~1948–1953). He subsequently held a faculty post at the University of Chicago from ~1953 to 2003.
